issues.name: acli-jira-incorrect-action-flag-syntax
issues.title: Used deprecated --action flag syntax instead of acli subcommand pattern
issues.description: The assistant ran `acli jira --action getIssueList --jql "..."` which immediately failed with 'unknown flag: --action'. The acli CLI uses a modern subcommand pattern: `acli jira workitem search --jql "..." --fields "..."`. This caused a command failure and required iterative help-command discovery before the correct syntax was found.

issues.name: browser-first-before-acli-cli-available
issues.title: Attempted browser automation before checking available CLI tools
issues.description: When asked 'show my jira tickets', the assistant first tried to use the Chrome browser extension (mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp) which timed out after 13 seconds with 'No Chrome extension connected'. Only after that failure did the assistant pivot to using acli. The user had acli available and a CLI-focused approach should have been tried first.

issues.name: iterative-help-command-discovery-acli
issues.title: Three sequential --help calls required to discover correct acli syntax after failure
issues.description: After the --action flag error, the assistant ran three sequential help commands (acli jira --help, acli jira workitem --help, acli jira workitem search --help) to discover the correct syntax. This multi-step discovery could be avoided if the correct syntax were known upfront, saving 3 extra round trips and approximately 10 seconds.

issues.name: jira-ticket-listing-automation
issues.title: Repeatable Jira ticket listing workflow can be automated with a direct skill
issues.description: The user's request 'show my jira tickets' is a clear, high-frequency task that requires no clarification and always maps to the same acli command pattern. A skill that directly executes `acli jira workitem search --jql "assignee = currentUser() AND resolution = Unresolved ORDER BY priority DESC" --fields "key,summary,priority,status"` would eliminate all the failed attempts and discovery steps.
